Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The test `testUnionOfVariableAndNode` fails with the exception "Cannot compare pointers that do not belong to the same tree," which occurs when evaluating the XPath expression "$var | /MAIN/A". The exception originates in the `NodePointer.compareNodePointers` method at line 665. The code checks if two NodePointers belong to the same tree by walking up their parent pointers. When it cannot reconcile the trees, it throws the mentioned exception.

The XPath expression combines a variable `$var` and node-set `/MAIN/A`. The variable `$var` is declared as a simple string variable in the test (`"varValue"`), whereas `/MAIN/A` points to XML nodes. The pointers returned by `iteratePointers("$var | /MAIN/A")` iterate over both the variable and the nodes.

The issue arises because these pointers come from different "trees": the variable pointer and the node pointer do not share a common root node structure. The comparison logic in `compareNodePointers` expects both NodePointers to come from the same XML tree structure so they can be ordered or compared properly. But in reality, the variable pointer points to a separate context (variable store), causing the exception.

Thus, the bug occurs because the union operator (`|`) processing leads to comparing pointers belonging to different underlying tree contexts (a variable pointer vs an XML node pointer), which the current implementation does not handle gracefully. This results in the `JXPathException` when their pointers are compared.

The root cause is that the pointer comparison logic lacks support for cross-context comparison involving variables and nodes. The union operation and related pointer iteration must either avoid comparing such heterogeneous pointers or be enhanced to support comparing pointers that belong to different data sources.

Recent bug reports do not appear relevant to this specific pointer comparison issue.

Summary:
- The XPath union expression includes a variable and XML nodes.
- Variables and nodes produce pointers from different tree contexts.
- `compareNodePointers` expects pointers in the same tree and throws when not.
- The failure in the test reveals missing handling for union of variable and node pointers.
- Fix requires improving pointer comparison or union evaluation to handle mixed sources.

This diagnosis uses the failing test, the pointer comparison method source, and observed symptoms from the exception stack and test code.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
